walkthroughs.body_html:
A series circuit has one loop. Current goes through every component in turn.

Add more bulbs in series - they all get dimmer because each gets less voltage.

If one bulb breaks, all the bulbs go out. Like old Christmas lights!

Current is the same everywhere in a series circuit.

A parallel circuit has branches - each component sits on its own loop.

Each branch gets the full voltage, so bulbs stay bright when you add more.

If one bulb breaks, the others keep working.

Houses are wired in parallel - that's why you can switch on one light without all of them turning on!

Every magnet has two ends: a North pole and a South pole.

The rule: Opposites attract, likes repel.

North + South: attract.
North + North: repel.
South + South: repel.

Magnetic materials: iron, steel, nickel, cobalt.

mcqs.q: In a parallel circuit, if one bulb breaks the others.
options: All go out
Get brighter
Keep working
Run out of charge

mcqs.q: Two north poles brought together will.
options: Attract
Repel
Do nothing
Stick like glue

mcqs.q: For a projectile launched horizontally, what affects the horizontal component of velocity during flight (ignoring air resistance)?
options: Nothing — horizontal velocity stays constant; only vertical velocity changes due to gravity.
Gravity slows down both the vertical and horizontal motion.
Because the plates are uniform in shape.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.

mcqs.q: When energy is 'lost' as heat due to friction, what has really happened?
options: Energy has been converted into mass following E=mc^2.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Energy has been transferred to the thermal store of the surroundings — it's not destroyed, just dissipated.
Energy has been used up and no longer exists.

mcqs.q: Why is the electric field between parallel charged plates considered uniform?
options: Because the plates are uniform in shape.
The horizontal velocity increases over time because the projectile is falling.
Field strength is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the region (away from edges), unlike the inverse-square field of a point charge.
The field still decreases with the inverse square of distance — uniform just means it's smooth.
